items.title: A 10-year Analysis of Plastic Surgery Training in Scotland: the Impact of COVID-19 and Subsequent Recovery.
items.summary: Plastic Surgery training within the UK requires exposure to a defined set of elective and emergency indicative procedures, listed in the curriculum produced by the ISCP. Past and present Scottish trainee operative exposure has not previously been objectively quantified.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Effect of Tongue Suture on Post-Operative Course After Palatoplasty
items.summary: Airway compromise is a concern following palatoplasty. A tongue suture may be placed to provide forward tongue traction during airway compromise, but its clinical benefit and potential impact on postoperative feeding remains uncertain.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Response to: Correspondence on “Methodological quality and performance of artificial intelligence and machine learning models for preoperative risk prediction in plastic surgery: A systematic review”
items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: To Give or Not to Give; A Retrospective Cohort Study Assessing the Role of Prophylactic Antibiotics in Reducing SSI Following Excision of Ulcerated Skin Cancer
items.summary: The study aims to assess the effectiveness of prophylactic antibiotics in reducing surgical site infection (SSI) rates after excision of ulcerated skin cancer.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Normative Reference Values for the LYMQOL Upper and Lower Extremity Modules: A Population-Based Benchmarking Study for Outcomes after Lymphedema Treatment and Reconstruction
items.summary: The LYMQOL is a lymphedema-specific patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) designed to assess quality of life (QoL) across function, appearance, symptoms and mood, and global quality of life in individuals with upper- (UL) and lower-limb (LL) lymphedema.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Changes in Earnings and Employment After Isolated Traumatic Upper Extremity Peripheral Nerve Injury
items.summary: Following traumatic upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries, the functional limitations and prolonged recovery can lead to time away from work, reduced productivity, and long-term economic consequences.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: “Limiting Donor-Site Morbidity in Autograft Nerve Reconstruction: Sural Nerve With and Without TMR Compared to Motor Nerve to Vastus Lateralis”
items.summary: Substantial donor-site morbidity can occur when harvesting sensory nerves for autograft reconstruction. We hypothesized that using a lower extremity motor nerve or alternatively performing targeted muscle reinnervation (TMR) at the time of sural nerve harvest, would reduce morbidity.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Planning and Insetting Strategies to Optimize Outcomes in PAP Flap Breast Reconstruction
items.summary: The profunda artery perforator (PAP) flap has become an established alternative for autologous breast reconstruction when abdominal tissue is inadequate or undesirable. This study aimed to describe our institutional experience, focusing on preoperative perforator mapping, flap design, and insetting strategies.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Clinical Outcomes and Cost-Effectiveness of Subpectoral Implantation as Salvage Strategy for Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Pocket Infection: A Comparative Retrospective Study
items.summary: Complete system extraction is the gold standard for cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) infection, but procedural risks and costs often limit its feasibility in frail patients.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: BAPRAS @ 80
items.summary: As we celebrate the 80th anniversary of the British Association of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons (BAPRAS), I reflect with pride on our Association's history and with confidence in its future.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: “Is microsurgical autologous breast reconstruction safe in patients with a history of venous thromboembolism? A retrospective cohort study of 14,309 patients”- interpreting risk beyond statistical significance
items.summary: Lee et al. should be commended for examining an important and clinically intuitive question: whether a history of venous thromboembolism (VTE) identifies patients at greater postoperative risk after microsurgical autologous breast reconstruction. For reconstructive surgeons, the ques-tion is highly relevant.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: Which integrated plastic surgery residencies produce the most subspecialty fellows? Trends across subspecialty fellows from 2021–2025
items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study Determining the Effect of Perivascular Botulinum Toxin Injections for the Treatment of Post Traumatic Cold Intolerance
items.summary: To determine whether perivascular botulinum toxin injections can improve the symptoms of post traumatic cold intolerance.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Advancing Limb Preservation: A Vasculo-Ortho-Plastic Approach to the Diabetic Foot – A Narrative Review
items.summary: The global diabetic foot pandemic has led to a rising incidence of limb-threatening disease. Advances across vascular, orthopaedic, and plastic surgery now make functional limb salvage possible for patients who might previously have faced major amputation.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Cortical Burring in Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck with Narrow or Involved Deep Margins – A Series of 200 Patients
items.summary: Primary squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the head and neck with close or involved deep excision margins carries high risk of recurrence, necessitating adjuvant radiotherapy or bone burring and subsequent reconstruction. Minimal work has been published examining the role and efficacy of burring.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Endoscopic versus Open Gynecomastia Excision: A Retrospective Two-Center Comparative Study of Sensory, Aesthetic, and Patient-Reported Outcomes
items.summary: Endoscopic gynecomastia excision places the incision away from the nipple–areola complex (NAC) and may improve sensory and aesthetic outcomes. Comparative evidence incorporating objective sensory testing and patient-reported outcomes remains limited.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: Impact of neurodevelopmental disorders on surgical outcomes in patients with cleft lip and palate: A retrospective cohort study from the U.S. collaborative network
items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: "Methodological quality and performance of artificial intelligence and machine learning models for preoperative risk prediction in plastic surgery: A systematic review"
items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Pedicled Anatomical Fat Preservation Improves Multi-territory Perforator Flap Survival by Increasing Blood Supply via Arteriogenesis and Angiogenesis in Rats
items.summary: Improving multi-territory perforator flap survival is essential for reconstructing major defects. Although many methods have been used to increase flap survival, there is no widely adopted procedure.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Mapping the anatomic variation in double skin paddle ALT perforator flaps based on long-term clinical outcomes of 171 patients
items.summary: The double skin paddle anterolateral thigh (ALT) perforator flap is widely used for reconstructing extensive or non-adjacent defects while allowing primary donor-site closure, yet anatomical variations in perforator convergence remain poorly characterized due to limited sample sizes in previous studies.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Histopathologic patterns of iatrogenic arterial wall injury in thrombosed free-flap microanastomoses
items.summary: Vascular thrombosis remains the leading cause of free-flap failure despite advances in microsurgical technique. The structural alterations underlying thrombosed human microanastomoses remain poorly characterized because surgically retrieved specimens are exceptionally rare.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Direct-to-implant or Two-stage Breast Reconstruction in Pathogenic Mutations Carriers after Risk-reducing Nipple-sparing Mastectomy: A Real-World Multicenter Cohort
items.summary: Nipple-sparing mastectomy (NSM) with immediate implant-based reconstruction has become a preferred strategy for patients with pathogenic germline variant (PV) undergoing risk-reducing mastectomy (RRM).
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Extended Reality-Assisted Preoperative Simulation for DIEP Flap Harvest Improves Interobserver Reliability of Perforator Identification
items.summary: Deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flap reconstruction requires precise understanding of the highly variable vascular anatomy.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Craniofacial Anatomy and Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Systematic Review of Anatomical Associations, Airway Changes, and Functional Outcomes
items.summary: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is common in individuals with craniofacial syndromes, but the anatomical features that distinguish patients with OSA from those without remains poorly defined.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Selective Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Oncologic Skin Graft Reconstruction
items.summary: Skin grafting is frequently required following oncologic skin cancer excision when direct closure or local flaps are not feasible. Surgical site infection (SSI) is a major cause of graft failure; however, the role of prophylactic oral antibiotics remains uncertain.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Refining Breast Reconstruction: Impact of Polyurethane Coating on Prepectoral Reconstruction Outcomes
items.summary: In prepectoral breast reconstruction (PBR), implant coverage with acellular dermal matrix (ADM) is standard but costly and associated with complications. Polyurethane (PU)-coated implants represent a potential alternative, yet clinical evidence in the prepectoral setting remains limited.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Invited commentary on ‘Palatal microcirculation in minimal-incision cleft palate repair: Impact of lateral releasing incisions: A controlled intraoperative study’: The next steps to improve the results in cleft palate surgery
items.summary: The authors are to be praised for highlighting the effects of surgical manoeuvres on the vascularity of the palate.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Segmental SMAS tensioning in deep plane rhytidectomy to improve muscle dynamics and cosmetic outcomes
items.summary: Deep plane facelifting effectively repositions ptotic facial and cervical tissues, but persistent SMAS laxity, reduced spanning tension, and volume loss can limit midface, perioral, and jawline improvement.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: “A novel workflow for three-dimensional and longitudinal analysis of craniofacial morphology and its application to syndromic bilateral coronal synostosis after Endoscope-Assisted Suturectomy”
items.summary: Quantitative evaluation of craniofacial morphology remains challenging because the orbital and frontal regions are three-dimensionally complex.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Automatic Three-Dimensional Surface Imaging with Chest Computerized Alignment for Preoperative Breast Volume Evaluation
items.summary: Accurate breast volume assessment is essential for preoperative planning in unilateral one-stage immediate breast reconstruction to achieve symmetry and optimal cosmetic outcomes. However, no standard method for precise breast volume estimation has been established.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Skeletal relapse and associated factors during the consolidation period following mandibular distraction osteogenesis in craniofacial microsomia: a retrospective cohort study
items.summary: Skeletal relapse following mandibular distraction osteogenesis (MDO) in craniofacial microsomia (CFM) remains challenging, yet the extent of relapse in the distraction region during the consolidation period and its associated predictors remain underexplored.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: The surgical management of radiation induced angiosarcoma of the breast: The Newcastle experience
items.summary: Radiation induced angiosarcoma of the breast is a rare but aggressive malignancy arising from the endothelial cells of blood or lymphatic vessels, typically in the context of previous radiotherapy for breast cancer.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: “Early Experience with Single-Axillary-Incision Endoscopic Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy and Immediate DIEP Flap Breast Reconstruction”
items.summary: Endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy (ENSM) has been increasingly adopted to improve cosmetic outcomes while maintaining oncologic safety. However, most ENSM reconstructions remain implant-based, and data on autologous reconstruction—particularly deep inferior epigastric artery perforator (DIEP) flaps—are limited.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Bridging Policy and Practice: Recommendations for Parental Support in Plastic Surgery
items.summary: Pregnancy, parental leave, and lactation remain challenging for surgical trainees, yet specialty-specific data in plastic and reconstructive surgery (PRS) are limited.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: High-risk cosmetic procedures: what crackdown means for nurses
items.summary: Leading cosmetic nurses have welcomed proposals from the government to “crack down on cosmetic cowboys” by introducing new restrictions on who can perform high-risk procedures.
items.source: Nursing Times

items.title: Government sets out detail of crackdown on cosmetic procedures
items.summary: The Government has set out proposals for limiting who can carry out high-risk cosmetic procedures such as liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), vampire facials and chemical peels.
items.source: Pulse Today

items.title: Robot-assisted (super) microsurgery: a randomized in vivo preclinical trial for microvascular anastomosis
items.summary: Microsurgery's requirement for extraordinary surgical skill, physical endurance, and prolonged training impedes widespread clinical implementation. This study evaluated objective histological metrics and subjective parameters of a multi-modular microsurgical robotic system in a rat model.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Which Motor Branch to Use? Targeted Muscle Reinnervation for Digital Neuromas: An Anatomical Study
items.summary: Symptomatic neuromas following digital nerve injury frequently cause persistent pain and impaired hand function.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Exceptional Referral Protocol: Primary Vetting Outcomes in the East of Scotland Following the Introduction of Clinical Photography.
items.summary: The NHS Scotland Exceptional Referral Protocol (ERP), recently renamed the National Referral Protocol (NRP)(SGHD CMO (2025) 17), provides a pathway for patients seeking body-altering procedures where there is an aesthetic element.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: “Long-term results of 149 free fibula flap reconstructions in extensive limb defects: Experiences from nine European hospitals”
items.summary: Dear Editors…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: “Management of severe post-burn deformities of the hand.”
items.summary: To the Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: Complications and health costs of cosmetic tourism. A systematic review
items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Breast surgery guides offer a decision-making framework for gynaecomastia and congenital breast asymmetry procedures
items.summary: GIRFT breast surgery guides set out a decision-making framework for gynaecomastia and congenital breast asymmetry procedures.
items.source: Hub intelligence

items.title: Quality of life after mastectomy alone compared with subpectoral breast reconstruction using the BREAST-Q and RAND-36
items.summary: Mastectomy can negatively affect health-related quality of life (HR-QoL). Subpectoral breast reconstruction can be performed to restore breast contour and may improve HR-QoL. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term impact of mastectomy alone compared with subpectoral breast reconstruction.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: “Advancing Gender-Affirming Surgery Medicare Policies in Canada: A Qualitative Description Study”
items.summary: Gender-affirming surgery (GAS) is one component of gender-affirming care. Access to GAS in Canada remains inconsistent due to jurisdictional differences in GAS policies.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Quantitative Analysis of Tissue Oxygenation Trajectories in DIEP Flaps Using Near Infrared Spectroscopy – A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.summary: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is an adjunct for monitoring breast free flaps. There is a paucity of studies using large NIRS datasets to characterize how patient-, flap-, and operative-level factors and systemic hemodynamics influence postoperative StO₂.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Unilateral Macrostomia Repair with Modified Muscle Reconstruction: Long-term Anthropometric Evaluation of Static and Smile Symmetry
items.summary: Macrostomia, or transverse facial cleft, significantly impairs facial aesthetics and oral function. While various repair techniques have been reported, achieving satisfactory bilateral symmetry, particularly during dynamic expressions such as smiling, remains a challenge.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Impact of diabetes mellitus on clinical outcome in burns patients managed in a national burns centre
items.summary: The impact of diabetes mellitus on outcomes following burn injury remains unclear. This study aimed to characterise diabetic burn patients and their outcomes at a national burns centre.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery
